an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; this ticket's ACs cover the BEHIND refresh path only. Left untouched deliberately — flag for a follow-up if placeholder-pinned fork PRs appear in live traces.

item field → fresh github_get_pr] PROBE -->|unknown| DEFER[defer, fail closed
re-probe next tick] PROBE -->|false| PARK[fork park: validation_failed
zero attempts/markers — AC2] PROBE -->|true| FETCH[clone base, fetch refs/pull/N/head
merge origin/main] FETCH --> PUSH[push HEAD:branch → fork token URL
never the base — AC1] PUSH -->|fails × MAX| PARK2[guest-style park — AC3
not silent-update-degraded] PUSH -->|head moves| RESET[gh-994 head-change reset
clears validation_failed] ```

### Thread 1 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 338

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2072

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

Same note for `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure`, which mirrors `recordSilentUpdateFailure` — there the divergence is deliberate (guest park vs degraded label), so a shared helper is less pressing, but the marker-trail counting half is identical.

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same-tick double park when the red-head park already fired**

`forkSilentUpdateGate` parks a non-editable fork only when `(ticket.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') === -1` — but `ticket.labels` is the **tick-start payload snapshot**. Earlier in this same pass the red-head park (the `headChecksRed` block above) may already have added `validation_failed` and posted its own park comment — the snapshot doesn't reflect that. Not worth heavy machinery — options: thread the same-pass park state (there is already an `unparkedThisPass` precedent) into the gate, or have `parkForkGuest` skip the comment when the label was added earlier in this pass. Rare corner; comment spam only.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Thread 1 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 338

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2072

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

ghPrMaintainerCanModify: smProviderReal().ghPrMaintainerCanModify,

```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; # pr-1072: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park) ## Description Closes #1070 ### What changed `update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull//head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush. ### Key decisions - **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; this ticket's ACs cover the BEHIND refresh path only. Left untouched deliberately — flag for a follow-up if placeholder-pinned fork PRs appear in live traces.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD PR[BEHIND fork PR] --> GATE{forkHeadFull?} GATE -->|same-repo| BASE[classic base repush — AC4 unchanged] GATE -->|fork| PROBE[maintainerCanModify probe
item field → fresh github_get_pr] PROBE -->|unknown| DEFER[defer, fail closed
re-probe next tick] PROBE -->|false| PARK[fork park: validation_failed
zero attempts/markers — AC2] PROBE -->|true| FETCH[clone base, fetch refs/pull/N/head
merge origin/main] FETCH --> PUSH[push HEAD:branch → fork token URL
never the base — AC1] PUSH -->|fails × MAX| PARK2[guest-style park — AC3
not silent-update-degraded] PUSH -->|head moves| RESET[gh-994 head-change reset
clears validation_failed] ```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json

### Thread 1 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 338

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2072

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

Same note for `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure`, which mirrors `recordSilentUpdateFailure` — there the divergence is deliberate (guest park vs degraded label), so a shared helper is less pressing, but the marker-trail counting half is identical.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1072 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1072 - **Title**: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1070` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +653 - **Deletions**: -15 - **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-18T22:29:24Z ## PR Description Closes #1070 ### What changed `update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull//head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush. ### Key decisions - **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; this ticket's ACs cover the BEHIND refresh path only. # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1072._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 338

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2072

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

# pr-1072: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park) ## Description Closes #1070 ### What changed `update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull//head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush. ### Key decisions - **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; this ticket's ACs cover the BEHIND refresh path only. Left untouched deliberately — flag for a follow-up if placeholder-pinned fork PRs appear in live traces.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD PR[BEHIND fork PR] --> GATE{forkHeadFull?} GATE -->|same-repo| BASE[classic base repush — AC4 unchanged] GATE -->|fork| PROBE[maintainerCanModify probe
item field → fresh github_get_pr] PROBE -->|unknown| DEFER[defer, fail closed
re-probe next tick] PROBE -->|false| PARK[fork park: validation_failed
zero attempts/markers — AC2] PROBE -->|true| FETCH[clone base, fetch refs/pull/N/head
merge origin/main] FETCH --> PUSH[push HEAD:branch → fork token URL
never the base — AC1] PUSH -->|fails × MAX| PARK2[guest-style park — AC3
not silent-update-degraded] PUSH -->|head moves| RESET[gh-994 head-change reset
clears validation_failed] ```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Thread 1 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 338

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; # PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 338

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2072

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

Same note for `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure`, which mirrors `recordSilentUpdateFailure` — there the divergence is deliberate (guest park vs degraded label), so a shared helper is less pressing, but the marker-trail counting half is identical.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2478

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same-tick double park when the red-head park already fired**

`forkSilentUpdateGate` parks a non-editable fork only when `(ticket.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') === -1` — but `ticket.labels` is the **tick-start payload snapshot**. Earlier in this same pass the red-head park (the `headChecksRed` block above) may already have added `validation_failed` and posted its own park comment — the snapshot doesn't reflect that. In that corner (guest fork with red checks AND maintainer edits off) the PR receives **two different park comments in one tick** (label add is idempotent, so no label churn; next tick's fresh payload suppresses further repeats).

Not worth heavy machinery — options: thread the same-pass park state (there is already an `unparkedThisPass` precedent) into the gate, or have `parkForkGuest` skip the comment when the label was added earlier in this pass. Rare corner; comment spam only.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` line 3343

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicated stub property**

# pr-1072: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park) ## Description Closes #1070 ### What changed `update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull//head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush. ### Key decisions - **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; this ticket's ACs cover the BEHIND refresh path only. Left untouched deliberately — flag for a follow-up if placeholder-pinned fork PRs appear in live traces.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD PR[BEHIND fork PR] --> GATE{forkHeadFull?} GATE -->|same-repo| BASE[classic base repush — AC4 unchanged] GATE -->|fork| PROBE[maintainerCanModify probe
item field → fresh github_get_pr] PROBE -->|unknown| DEFER[defer, fail closed
re-probe next tick] PROBE -->|false| PARK[fork park: validation_failed
zero attempts/markers — AC2] PROBE -->|true| FETCH[clone base, fetch refs/pull/N/head
merge origin/main] FETCH --> PUSH[push HEAD:branch → fork token URL
never the base — AC1] PUSH -->|fails × MAX| PARK2[guest-style park — AC3
not silent-update-degraded] PUSH -->|head moves| RESET[gh-994 head-change reset
clears validation_failed] ```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1072 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1072 - **Title**: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1070` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +653 - **Deletions**: -15 - **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:56:52Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-18T22:29:24Z ## PR Description Closes #1070 ### What changed `update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull//head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush. ### Key decisions - **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; this ticket's ACs cover the BEHIND refresh path only. Left untouched deliberately — flag for a follow-up if placeholder-pinned fork PRs appear in live traces.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD PR[BEHIND fork PR] --> GATE{forkHeadFull?} GATE -->|same-repo| BASE[classic base repush — AC4 unchanged] GATE -->|fork| PROBE[maintainerCanModify probe
item field → fresh github_get_pr] PROBE -->|unknown| DEFER[defer, fail closed
re-probe next tick] PROBE -->|false| PARK[fork park: validation_failed
zero attempts/markers — AC2] PROBE -->|true| FETCH[clone base, fetch refs/pull/N/head
merge origin/main] FETCH --> PUSH[push HEAD:branch → fork token URL
never the base — AC1] PUSH -->|fails × MAX| PARK2[guest-style park — AC3
not silent-update-degraded] PUSH -->|head moves| RESET[gh-994 head-change reset
clears validation_failed] ```

### Thread 1 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 338

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: case-sensitive same-repo comparison can misroute a base PR into the fork paths**

`forkHeadFull` decides "same repo vs fork" with a case-sensitive string compare:

```javascript
return (full.indexOf('/') !== -1 && full !== baseFull) ? full : null;
```

GitHub repository names are case-insensitive. The base side comes from config (`effectiveRepoInfo.owner/repo`), while `headRepoFull` comes from the API's `head.repo.full_name` — if the two spell the same repository with different casing (e.g. config `istin/dmtools-agents` vs API `IstiN/dmtools-agents`), a **same-repo** PR is classified as a fork:

- AC4 is silently violated (the probe API call is paid, and the refresh goes through the `refs/pull` fetch + merge + `HEAD:<branch>` push instead of the byte-identical base repush).
- Worse: if such a PR carries `maintainer_can_modify=false`, `forkSilentUpdateRoute` sends it to the **park path** — a healthy same-repo PR gets a false guest park and stops receiving validation CI until a human pushes.

This is exactly the class of silent misroute the gh-1059 shared-resolver work was eliminating. Cheap fix — normalize both sides:

```javascript
var full = String(headRepoFull || '').toLowerCase();
var baseFull = (String(baseOwner || '') + '/' + String(baseRepo || '')).toLowerCase();
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2072

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: forkSilentUpdateBranch duplicates the classic silent-update command chain**

`forkSilentUpdateBranch` (clone → fetch → ancestor-check → merge → token-URL push) re-implements ~80% of `silentUpdateBranch`'s shell chain a few screens up. The two have already drifted in incidentally (clone shape, comment text) and will keep drifting — e.g. the next silent-update hardening (timeout, depth, `--no-edit` flags, new skip conditions) must be hand-copied to both. Consider extracting one command builder parameterized by (a) how the head is obtained (`--single-branch --branch <b>` vs `refs/pull/<N>/head` fetch) and (b) the push target URL, so the shared ancestor-check/merge/push skeleton exists once.

Same note for `recordForkSilentUpdateFailure`, which mirrors `recordSilentUpdateFailure` — there the divergence is deliberate (guest park vs degraded label), so a shared helper is less pressing, but the marker-trail counting half is identical.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js` line 2478

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: same-tick double park when the red-head park already fired**

`forkSilentUpdateGate` parks a non-editable fork only when `(ticket.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') === -1` — but `ticket.labels` is the **tick-start payload snapshot**. Earlier in this same pass the red-head park (the `headChecksRed` block above) may already have added `validation_failed` and posted its own park comment — the snapshot doesn't reflect that. In that corner (guest fork with red checks AND maintainer edits off) the PR receives **two different park comments in one tick** (label add is idempotent, so no label churn; next tick's fresh payload suppresses further repeats).

Not worth heavy machinery — options: thread the same-pass park state (there is already an `unparkedThisPass` precedent) into the gate, or have `parkForkGuest` skip the comment when the label was added earlier in this pass. Rare corner; comment spam only.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicated stub property**

```javascript
ghPrHeadRepoFull: smProviderReal().ghPrHeadRepoFull,
ghPrMaintainerCanModify: smProviderReal().ghPrMaintainerCanModify,
ghPrMaintainerCanModify: smProviderReal().ghPrMaintainerCanModify
```

`ghPrMaintainerCanModify` appears twice in this stub object — harmless in JS (last write wins) but it reads as a copy-paste slip and will confuse the next editor. Drop the duplicate line.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# pr-1072: gh-1070 [GOAL] Fork-aware silent-update: machine refreshes guest PR heads via maintainer-edit push (probe maintainerCanModify fall back to guest park) ## Description Closes #1070 ### What changed `update_branch`'s silent refresh is now fork-aware (gh-1070): a cross-repo PR head is probed for `maintainerCanModify` before any update attempt — an editable fork gets main merged into its fork branch via the maintainer-edit push (`refs/pull//head` fetch → merge `origin/main` → push `HEAD:` to the fork's token URL), a non-editable fork parks guest-style with zero attempts and zero bookkeeping, and same-repo PRs ride the untouched base repush. ### Key decisions - **Pure dispatch** in `validationLiveness` (`forkSilentUpdateRoute` → `base` / `fork` / `park`, `forkPushTokenUrl`) — the three-path routing is unit-testable without scm stubs (UT-1/UT-2); `smAgent` only probes and executes. - **One shared resolver** `smProvider.ghPrMaintainerCanModify` (REST `maintainer_can_modify` + GraphQL `maintainerCanModify` dialects, `null` when absent) consumed by `githubSource` on the PR item — the gh-1059 no-drift pattern; an unknown probe fails **closed to the park path**, never an unprobed attempt. - **AC3 race**: a push that fails despite the probe rides the existing silent-update marker trail (counted once per tick, re-probe next tick); after MAX consecutive failures the PR parks **guest-style** (`validation_failed` + `parked-head:` comment) — never `silent-update-degraded` (the workspace is not dead, the permission is gone). - **Park reset parity**: the gh-757 guest park records `parked-head: `, so the gh-994 head-change reset clears it on any author push; a reset in the same tick yields to the re-query instead of re-parking. - **AC4**: same-repo heads return `route: 'base'` without even paying the probe API call; the base repush command is byte-identical to the pre-gh-1070 form (regression test pins it). ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js # full suite (run_all.json manifest): 4531 passed, 0 failed ``` New coverage: routing dialects (UT-1), fork push URL never targets the base (UT-2), non-editable park with zero markers (UT-3/AC2), end-to-end BEHIND fork refresh + park clear (IT-1/AC1), AC3 exhaustion loop over 4 simulated ticks, same-repo regression (AC4), two-fork mixed tick. ### Known residual (out of scope) The gh-852 placeholder-reset lane still uses the classic base-only `silentUpdateBranchTracked`; this ticket's ACs cover the BEHIND refresh path only. Left untouched deliberately — flag for a follow-up if placeholder-pinned fork PRs appear in live traces.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD PR[BEHIND fork PR] --> GATE{forkHeadFull?} GATE -->|same-repo| BASE[classic base repush — AC4 unchanged] GATE -->|fork| PROBE[maintainerCanModify probe
item field → fresh github_get_pr] PROBE -->|unknown| DEFER[defer, fail closed
re-probe next tick] PROBE -->|false| PARK[fork park: validation_failed
zero attempts/markers — AC2] PROBE -->|true| FETCH[clone base, fetch refs/pull/N/head
merge origin/main] FETCH --> PUSH[push HEAD:branch → fork token URL
never the base — AC1] PUSH -->|fails × MAX| PARK2[guest-style park — AC3
not silent-update-degraded] PUSH -->|head moves| RESET[gh-994 head-change reset
clears validation_failed] ```
